title: Enterprise inference playbook - platform teams (draft)
content:
One-line: Quick playbook for pitching Redwood Inference to internal platform teams and central infra owners. Purpose: create a short deck (10-12 slides) + one-page battlecard for platform PMs/infra leads evaluating inference runtimes, with emphasis on integration cost, SLO guarantees, and migration risk reduction.

Slide outline (working):
1) Cover / TL;DR — Redwood as unified inference runtime: hosted + dedicated + private. Hook: shave 15-40% off per-token cost while preserving latency SLOs; reduce ops burden for model rollouts.
2) Who this helps — Platform teams that must: manage multi-tenant ML workloads, enforce RBAC/KMS, provide internal SLAs to product teams.
3) Tech win conditions — what matters to platform owners:
   - Predictable p95 latency under mixed batch sizes
   - Cost per 1k tokens predictable + knob to throttle cost spikes
   - Easy model pinning and canary rollouts across environments
   - Central observability: token-level breakdowns, per-route dashboards
4) Value props — quick bullets for a slide:
   - Unified API that maps to hosted/dedicated/private deployments (same dev UX)
   - SLA-backed dedicated pools and autoscaling policies for predictable throughput
   - Native KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs for compliance
   - Intelligent batching and caching reduces ECU/GPU spend; configuration suggestions from Redwood Optimize
5) Typical buying group & their concerns
   - Platform lead (decision owner): cost predictability, security, multi-tenant isolation
   - SRE/infra (technical evaluator): autoscaling, SLOs, fallback policies
   - ML platform/ML engineer: latency, model rollout, KV cache management
   - Procurement/security: licensing, legal, SOC/ISO docs
6) Demonstration checklist (for POC) — 20–30min demo path:
   - Quick API call (hosted) to show parity with existing open models
   - Swap to dedicated pool with same API key (show migration pain reduced)
   - Show per-route latency/cost dashboard and trace a slow request
   - Execute a canary rollback after a synthetic regression (demo of rollouts)
   - Show KMS-encryption and audit log entry for a request
7) Competitive frame (how to win the convo)
   - Vs hyperscalers: emphasize inference economics, model-agnostic tuning, and unified tooling (avoid re-architecting across clouds)
   - Vs self-hosted open-source runtimes: emphasize operational burden reduction, SLA, and features like intelligent routing + fallback variants
   - Vs other inference vendors: highlight private deployment story (VPC + on-prem) and observability granularity
8) Pricing levers to discuss with procurement
   - Hosted: per-token consumption + optional reserved commit for steady-state workloads
   - Dedicated: monthly reserved capacity, burst options, predictable billing for platform budgets
   - Private: license + support + optional managed upgrade path
   - Cost levers: batching config, KV cache reuse, quantization profile suggestions (show concrete %s from recent benchmarks: 18-35% token-cost reduction on e2e reranking workloads)
9) Objection handling - short scripts
   - "We can just use cloud provider endpoints" -> "Totally — many customers keep baseline cloud endpoints for dev, but use Redwood for predictable production throughput, lower per-token cost, and standardized rollouts across models/regions. We can show a migration plan and cost model in 2 weeks."
   - "Security/compliance concerns" -> "We offer Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) with KMS/HSM and audit logs; we can provide SOC2 docs and run a short security review with your SecOps."
   - "Vendor lock-in" -> "API parity, model-agnostic tooling, and exportable audit + model version metadata reduce lock-in. We help plan an export/restore path in the SOW."
10) Quick architecture slide (talking points)
   - Control plane (Redwood managed) for model catalog, rollouts, metrics + customer-managed data plane for private deployments
   - Smart routing and fallback: route by cost/latency/region with automatic fallback to cheaper compatible variant
   - Prefix/KV caching and continuous batching to minimize token compute
11) POC success metrics (mutually agreed)
   - p95 latency <= existing internal SLO or within +20ms
   - cost per 1M tokens reduced by target % (TBD per workload)
   - Successful canary rollout and rollback in <30 minutes
   - Audit logs and KMS proof-of-concept validated by security team
12) Next steps / ask
   - 1-week discovery: collect sample traffic, list of critical models, SLO targets (owner: platform lead)
   - 2-week POC: spin a dedicated pool, run 2x traffic replay, review cost/latency and rollback tests
   - Decision criteria: SLA accept, security sign-off, cost delta within agreed threshold

Battlecard one-pager (for SDRs/AE quick reference) — single slide condensed:
- Elevator: "Deploy inference predictably at scale — one API for hosted, dedicated, and private. Reduce per-token spend and ops overhead while keeping latency SLOs."
- 3 quick wins to call out: predictable p95, audit/KMS for compliance, canary + rollback in control plane
- 5 quick facts to memorize:
   * Dedicated pools: SLA-backed uptime
   * Private option: VPC & on-prem + KMS/HSM
   * Optimize: automatic batching/caching suggestions
   * Observability: token-level cost + route dashboards
   * Migration model: same API across environments
- Top objections + one-line responses (see slide 9)
- Demo play: 20 min: API call -> switch to dedicated -> show dashboard -> run canary rollback

Notes, open Qs, TODOs (working brain-dump):
- TODO: add recent benchmark numbers from infer-bench (ENG-4821) for 8k and 16k seqs. Evan to provide by 2026-01-15.
- Open Q: legal needs for some EU customers for on-prem templates (Maya to sync with legal: DOC-134).
- Need a short one-pager for procurement: sample SOW + price bands for 100k/1M/10M tokens per month.
- Add snippet of CLI commands for dedicated pool provisioning (Jordan to draft).
- Remove / slim feature list for SDR-facing one-pager — too much detail now.

Linked resources + demo artifacts:
- POC checklist doc (internal): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/GO/POC+-+Platform+Teams
- Sample cost model sheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1MockSheetExample
- ENG benchmark PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serve/pull/789

Style notes for final deck:
- Keep slides intentionally sparse: one headline + 3 bullets per slide for exec consumption
- Use a comparison table only in follow-up appendix (don’t start the demo with it)
- Include an appendix with integration steps and a 30/60/90 day plan for the platform team

Last edited by: Ava Thompson (notes). This is a working draft — expect churn. Use this as the master for the next go-to-market play iteration rather than duplicating.

Quick contact: ava.thompson@redwood.ai (for clarifying POC scope)
